description: GitHub Actions OIDC tokens against Azure Entra FLEXIBLE federated-identity-credential expressions (azure-fic-flexible) -- PREVIEW (Microsoft Learn page ms.date 2026-08-14, updated 2026-08-17; languageVersion always 1; Microsoft Graph / Azure portal only; application objects only). Flexible FIC replaces classic FIC's exact `subject` string with a `claimsMatchingExpression` (the two are mutually exclusive -- setting one nulls the other), written in a restricted language: `claims['<name>'] <op> '<comparand>'` clauses joined by `and`, where `eq` is exact and `matches` is a non-path-aware glob (`?` matches one character, `*` multiple, spanning `/` and `:` like AWS StringLike). Its purpose is to defeat classic FIC's cap of 20 credentials per identity by collapsing many exact credentials into one wildcard rule -- which is exactly what makes it trap-rich: the same `repo:org/*` that classic FIC treats as an inert literal here admits the whole org. For GitHub an expression may reference `sub`, `job_workflow_ref` (enabling the documented reusable-workflow `and` pin) and the two immutable id claims below; GitLab and Terraform Cloud flexible FIC support only `sub`. Because a rule lives in `claimsMatchingExpression` with `subject` null, a FIC check that inspects only the `subject` property is blind to it. [!] TWO TRANCHES, AND THE FIRST IS HISTORICAL. Microsoft revised this page on 2026-08-14 to make an immutable claim MANDATORY for GitHub. It now states, twice: \"GitHub expressions must match `sub` and at least one immutable claim\", and \"For GitHub, a flexible federated identity credential must match the `sub` claim and one or both of the following immutable claims: `repository_id` identifies the repository where the workflow runs. `repository_owner_id` identifies the repository owner. These claims are required regardless of whether `sub` uses a name-based, customized, or immutable format.\" The operator table restricts both id claims to `eq` (only `sub` and `job_workflow_ref` accept `matches`), and every documented example now carries `and claims['repository_id'] eq '456789'`. The eight 0.1.0 vectors were written against the 2026-06-15 revision and are all sub-only or sub+job_workflow_ref: their MATCH SEMANTICS are unchanged and still worth learning from, but as configurations they model a shape Entra now documents as invalid, so each is stamped. The 0.2.0 tranche carries the mandatory claim and is the current shape. Creation-time validity is deliberately NOT encoded in `expect` -- `expect` is the matcher's answer, and the per-issuer claim/operator allow-list is a configuration-validity concern the evaluator does not enforce (see ffl.py's scope cut) -- so it lives in vector prose, exactly as classic FIC's unvalidated-at-creation traps do in github-azure. [!] `matches` ANCHORING IS THE REFERENCE MATCHER'S READING, NOT A DOCUMENTED FACT. The cited page defines `matches` only as single-character (`?`) and multi-character (`*`) wildcard matching and is silent on whether the pattern must span the whole claim. ffl.py models it as anchored -- every documented example is a full-subject pattern, and a substring match would make the control meaningless -- and says so in its docstring; revisions of this description before 0.2.0 asserted \"anchored\" as bare fact, which it is not. Exactly one vector's declared result depends on it (gh-flex-question-width-excludes-longer), and that vector now carries the caveat.

vectors.description: The exact-match baseline in flexible form: claims['sub'] eq '...ref:refs/heads/main'. `eq` is byte-exact, so this is the classic single-branch pin re-expressed as an expression -- one branch of one repo, with no wildcard breadth. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: eq is exact, case-sensitive equality, so the expression admits exactly the main branch of exactly this repo -- the same tight boundary as a classic FIC subject, with no wildcard to widen it. The sub is name-based (it embeds the repository path).

vectors.description: The documented marquee use case -- claims['sub'] matches 'repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/*' -- collapsing a fleet of per-branch classic FICs into one credential. The `*` admits EVERY branch of the repo, matched here by a feature branch. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/feature-x

judgment.reason: Any branch of the repo satisfies the rule, so anyone who can push a branch -- not only a protected-branch maintainer -- runs a workflow that assumes this identity. The convenience that motivates flexible FIC (one rule for all branches) is the over-permission; scope the ref or add a second claim (job_workflow_ref or environment).

vectors.description: The wildcard classic FIC could not express: claims['sub'] matches 'repo:octo-org/*'. Because `matches` `*` is not path-aware (it spans `/` and `:`, like AWS StringLike), it admits every repo in the org at any ref -- the exact string classic Azure FIC treats as an inert literal (contrast az-fic-wildcard-is-literal-no-match). Matched here by a DIFFERENT repo than any specific one. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/another-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: Org-wide trust: every repository under octo-org, at every ref, assumes the identity, and a newly created repo inherits it immediately. `*` spanning the path and ref separators is the same non-path-aware breadth as AWS StringLike -- the difference is that flexible FIC HONORS it where classic FIC ignored it. Pin the repository, and prefer a claim bearing an immutable id where the issuer offers one.

vectors.description: The single-character wildcard's width trap: claims['sub'] matches '...ref:refs/heads/????'. `?` matches EXACTLY one character, so four of them match any four-character branch -- `main` here, but equally `test`, `temp`, or any attacker-pushed four-character branch -- while silently EXCLUDING the six-character `master` (see the sibling no-match gh-flex-question-width-excludes-longer). [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape. [!] This vector's declared result depends on `matches` being ANCHORED to the whole claim, which the cited page does not state -- it defines `matches` only as `?`/`*` wildcard matching. Under substring semantics this would come out the other way. The anchored reading is ffl.py's, documented in its docstring, and it is the reason for the result declared here.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: The width-counting `?` admits any four-character branch name -- not just the intended `main` but any `xxxx` branch an attacker can push -- while excluding longer intended branches. It encodes branch-name LENGTH, not identity: a footgun that reads as specificity. Match the ref name with eq, or a pattern anchored to the intended name.

vectors.description: The exclusion side of the `????` width trap: the same four-`?` pattern does not match the six-character branch `master`. `?` is exactly one character with no zero-or-more flex, so a length mismatch fails closed -- surprising when the author believed `????` meant 'any branch name'. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape. [!] This vector's declared result depends on `matches` being ANCHORED to the whole claim, which the cited page does not state -- it defines `matches` only as `?`/`*` wildcard matching. Under substring semantics this would come out the other way. The anchored reading is ffl.py's, documented in its docstring, and it is the reason for the result declared here.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/master

vectors.description: The `and` combinator on GitHub's two supported flexible-FIC claims -- the documented reusable-workflow scenario. claims['sub'] eq '...main' and claims['job_workflow_ref'] matches 'octo-org/reusable/.github/workflows/*@refs/heads/main' pins the CALLER (exact branch) AND the reusable workflow's repo and ref, in one credential classic FIC could not express (it matches a single subject only). job_workflow_ref is a GitHub-only flexible-FIC claim. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: A genuine improvement over classic FIC: two claims ANDed in one credential, pinning the caller branch and the reusable workflow's repo and ref. The residual is the `*` on the workflow FILENAME -- any workflow file under that path at refs/heads/main qualifies -- so a newly added or altered workflow in the reusable repo inherits trust. Pin the filename with eq if the set is closed.

vectors.description: The `and` guard working: the same expression as gh-flex-and-reusable-workflow-pin, but the reusable workflow ran on a DIFFERENT ref (@refs/heads/dev, not @refs/heads/main). The second clause's `matches` fails, so the conjunction fails and the exchange is refused -- the branch-pinned second claim catching what the caller sub alone could not. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: The conjunction fails closed on the second claim -- a reusable workflow invoked from the wrong ref cannot assume the identity even though the caller sub is exact. This is the value flexible FIC's `and` adds over classic single-subject FIC; the residual filename wildcard noted in the matching sibling still applies to workflows that DO run on the pinned ref.

vectors.description: The pull_request subject admitted via flexible FIC, plus a scanning blind spot. claims['sub'] eq 'repo:octo-org/octo-repo:pull_request' matches pull_request-triggered tokens (workflows running proposed changes before review/merge, not the protected default branch). Because flexible FIC sets the `subject` property to null and expresses matching in `claimsMatchingExpression` instead, any FIC check that inspects only the `subject` property cannot see this rule -- the over-permission is invisible to subject-based scanning. [!] 0.1.0 SHAPE, PRE-2026-08-14: this expression carries no immutable claim, and Entra now requires GitHub expressions to match `sub` plus `repository_id` and/or `repository_owner_id`. The match semantics below are unchanged and still hold; as a CONFIGURATION this is a shape the current page documents as invalid. See the 0.2.0 tranche for the same lesson in the current shape.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:pull_request

judgment.reason: The rule trusts pull_request-triggered runs, a classic OIDC over-permission: a pull_request workflow runs for a proposed change, not the protected default branch. The compounding risk is detectability: a scanner reading the FIC `subject` finds nothing, because flexible FIC nulls `subject` and puts the match in claimsMatchingExpression. Do not trust the pull_request subject; scanners must parse claimsMatchingExpression to cover flexible FIC.

vectors.description: The 0.2.0 baseline: the current documented shape, and the page's own `eq` example. claims['sub'] eq '...ref:refs/heads/main' and claims['repository_id'] eq '456789' -- exact branch AND the mandatory immutable claim. This is what gh-flex-eq-exact-branch has to become to be creatable after the 2026-08-14 revision, and the pair is worth reading together: the added clause changes nothing about WHICH tokens match here, only about whether Entra will accept the credential and what happens when the repository path is later reused.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: Both clauses are exact, so the expression admits exactly the main branch of exactly this repository, and `repository_id` pins that repository by an id which survives a rename -- the property the name-based sub lacks. Microsoft: "Use `repository_id` to bind the credential to a repository." The mandatory claim costs nothing here because the sub was already exact; this is the tight end of the range.

vectors.description: The marquee use case in its current, creatable form -- the shape of Microsoft's own `matches` example: claims['sub'] matches 'repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/*' and claims['repository_id'] eq '456789', matched here by a feature branch. The point of the vector is the contrast with gh-flex-matches-branch-wildcard: satisfying the new mandatory-claim rule makes the credential VALID, not SAFE.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/feature-x

judgment.reason: Identical breadth to the sub-only sibling: every branch of the repository still qualifies, so anyone who can push a branch runs a workflow that assumes this identity. `repository_id` constrains WHICH REPOSITORY, which the sub already named -- it buys rename-resistance, not ref scope. A reader who treats the now-mandatory immutable claim as the fix for wildcard breadth has drawn the wrong lesson from a rule that exists to defeat path reuse. Scope the ref, or add job_workflow_ref.

vectors.description: The mandatory claim satisfied in the way that helps least: claims['sub'] matches 'repo:octo-org/*' and claims['repository_owner_id'] eq '123456'. The rule permits `repository_owner_id` as the immutable claim ("one or both"), so this expression is documented-valid -- and it still admits every repository in the org at every ref, matched here by a DIFFERENT repo than any the author had in mind. Contrast gh-flex-matches-org-wide-wildcard, which is the same breadth without the claim.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/another-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: The immutable claim pins the OWNER, which is precisely the scope the wildcard already spans, so it constrains nothing the sub had not already conceded: every repository under the org, at every ref, with a newly created repo inheriting the trust immediately. The requirement is met and the breadth is untouched -- a credential can be fully compliant with the 2026-08-14 rule and still be the widest thing in the tenant. Microsoft's guidance splits the two jobs: "Use `repository_id` to bind the credential to a repository. Also match `repository_owner_id` when the repository must remain with a specific owner." Owner-only pinning is the second job done without the first.

vectors.description: What the mandatory claim actually buys, and the reason the rule exists. The sub is byte-identical to the pinned one -- whoever acquires the freed `octo-org/octo-repo` path after a delete or rename mints exactly this subject -- but the token's `repository_id` is the new repository's, not the pinned 456789. The conjunction fails and the exchange is refused, where the sub-only gh-flex-eq-exact-branch would have admitted it.
vectors.subject: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main

judgment.reason: Fails closed on the immutable clause while the name-based clause is fully satisfied -- the whole point of requiring an id claim "regardless of whether `sub` uses a name-based, customized, or immutable format". A name-based sub cannot distinguish the original repository from a later occupant of the same path; `repository_id` can, and `eq` is the only operator it accepts, so it cannot be loosened into a wildcard the way `sub` can.
